100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 28, 1926, British Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin called for a conference to address the growing tensions in the coal industry, aiming to avert a nationwide strike. In the United States, the Senate moved to discuss the ongoing debates surrounding Prohibition, with pressure mounting for potential reforms. Meanwhile, in Germany, political unrest continued as the government faced criticism for its handling of economic challenges.
